title: Regularity lifts from the quotient by a regular sequence
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a commutative Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], where local means having a unique maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$. Let $r\ge0$ and let $x_1,\ldots,x_r\in\mathfrak m$ be a regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence] in $R$. If the quotient ring $R/(x_1,\ldots,x_r)$ is regular local [def-weil-regular-scheme], then $R$ is regular local.

source.place: Tag 00NU, lemma-regular-mod-x, second assertion (including the empty sequence).

proof.text: Put I=(xs) and let q:R -> R/I be the canonical surjection. The regular local quotient is Noetherian, so choose a finite generating set s of its maximal ideal with cardinality equal to its spanFinrank. Choose a right inverse g of q, which exists by surjectivity, and put t=g(s). Then q(t)=s and |t| <= |s|. The image of the maximal ideal of R under q is the maximal ideal of R/I, by the local-ring maximal-ideal correspondence for a surjection.

source.place: Tag 00NU, lemma-regular-mod-x, generator-lifting argument; all sequence elements lifted at once using the Mathlib regular-sequence dimension formula.

proof.text: Since every element of xs belongs to the maximal ideal m of R, I <= m. The equality q(span(t))=q(m) implies span(t)+ker(q)=m+ker(q), by the ideal correspondence for a surjection. Substituting ker(q)=I and I <= m gives span(t union xs)=m. Consequently spanFinrank(m) <= |t union xs| <= |s|+length(xs) = spanFinrank(m_(R/I))+length(xs). This also applies when xs or s is empty; repetitions only decrease the cardinality.

source.place: Tag 00NU, lemma-regular-mod-x, generator-lifting argument; all sequence elements lifted at once using the Mathlib regular-sequence dimension formula.

proof.text: Regularity of R/I identifies spanFinrank(m_(R/I)) with ringKrullDim(R/I). Apply the Mathlib leaf lem-trf-regular-sequence-dimension-formula to the given regular sequence to get ringKrullDim(R/I)+length(xs)=ringKrullDim(R). Casting the generator bound to the extended dimension type yields spanFinrank(m) <= ringKrullDim(R). Mathlib IsRegularLocalRing.of_spanFinrank_maximalIdeal_le supplies the opposite dimension bound and proves that R is regular local. No successive quotient induction or separate finite-dimension reduction is necessary.
